approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including a direct formula-preserving exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon. It sanitizes and normalizes each identity, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even when its score worsens, while a separate archive retains the best observation. After each selected transition, memory keeps at most four inverse changes to rooted local motifs, balancing the two signs and favoring larger occurrence-count changes. Restrictions expire after four completed steps, overlapping keys receive the latest transition's provenance, and a veto requires both signs from one live transition. The repaired identity join is part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Prioritize the fraction of a motif's occurrences changed by the selected transition when choosing its limited inverse-memory attributes. A motif that disappears entirely or appears entirely new receives priority over a partly changed motif that also remains elsewhere in the molecule. This reallocates the same memory capacity toward more complete local-environment turnover; it does not assert that count turnover identifies a physical edit site. Earlier siblings withheld credit from nonimproving transitions, required every retained attribute to match, or preserved older overlapping origins. This experiment changes only which attributes receive credit within each selected transition, while retaining the Parent's credit eligibility, matching rule and memory lifecycle.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes its supplied panel with macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population standard deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its memory chooses attributes by absolute count change and then canonical motif order, without considering how many unchanged occurrences of that motif remain. A read-only reconstruction of its fifteen saved task logs reproduces all 435 installations, 1711 selected attributes and 195 vetoes among 4545 valid novel tests, with no reconstruction errors or obstruction releases. Of 3042 available changed-motif records, 286 retain occurrences on both sides of the transition; 206 such records receive one of the bounded memory slots. On the exact recorded transitions, the registered fractional-turnover ranking changes selected attribute sets at 94 installations, replacing 104 attributes while preserving every installation's total count and sign counts. Selected records with turnover below one fall from 206 to 104, and mean selected turnover rises from 0.9369819932648686 to 0.9681472822910578. Applying the two selection rules to separate latest-origin tables driven by that same accepted history changes 35 recorded candidate decisions in 30 batches and 11 sessions: 23 Parent vetoes become admissible and 12 Parent admissions become vetoes, for 184 versus 195 vetoes. These are unscored conditional memory comparisons, not a generated alternative walk or a claim about excluded scores. The exercised limitation is that limited inverse credit is spent partly on recurring environments when more completely changed environments compete for the same slots. Siblings n-a240f72e3717 and n-7c411fdf5a88 respectively changed transition eligibility and required complete signatures, activated, and lost paired means 0.020273360127168 and 0.039186838732539676. Sibling n-52759efc37a6 preserved overlapping origins, changed one complete batch and missed its score target. Their evidence makes a general fewer-vetoes claim untenable and leaves within-transition credit allocation unresolved.
hypothesis: Rank each selected transition's changed motifs first by absolute occurrence-count change divided by the larger of its before and after counts, then by the Parent's existing rank, so the unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse installation prioritizes complete motif turnover over partial changes to recurring motifs.

finding_summary.headline: Turnover-based memory redirected 26 scored batches, but the panel mean fell by 0.002456
finding_summary.insights: This rules out absent exposure, mere reordering and failure to change evaluated allocation as explanations for the missed score target. More complete turnover demonstrably changes which local attributes receive memory and which fresh molecules are tested. It also changes admissibility in both directions, so it is not a general relaxation of tabu. The full stream produced slightly more source improvements and archive improvements than the Parent, but their average positive gains were smaller; those event counts did not translate into better final search. The largest loss is not explained by rejecting the best immediate neighbor at the first divergence: in the affected sitagliptin seed, both runs chose the same next molecule after replacing a losing proposal, and their later histories separated. Nine of eleven first batch divergences similarly preserved the next state. Later archive gains are therefore evidence of actual descendants, not isolated causal rewards for particular retained motifs or missing alternatives. Turnover measures how much of a motif multiset changed, without identifying a physical edit site. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds and dense sulfur cages alongside more conventional aromatic families; the improved memory proxy has not established better chemical plausibility. The unresolved question is which local environments deserve exclusion for useful search, rather than whether fractional ranking can redirect it.
finding_summary.results: The new ranking changed the retained key set at 104 of 435 installations and replaced 114 attributes. On those same recorded transitions, mean selected occurrence turnover rose from 0.931289 under the old ranking to 0.965876, without reducing it at any installation or changing the number of slots assigned to either sign. Partly changed motifs occupied 110 of 1,707 slots, down from 221 under the old ranking. Separate memory histories on the recorded candidate stream yielded 28 newly admitted evaluated molecules and four new vetoes. Three vetoes caused evaluated replacements; one occurred beyond the alternative batch cutoff. This establishes changes to 26 complete scored batches. The recorded stream resolves all ten alternative legacy members in three of those batches; the other 23 alternatives remain incomplete. Among the 31 affected evaluated molecules, seven improved their source, one tied and 23 worsened it; six became next states and three immediately improved the archive. The complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519304, a paired change of -0.002456 against the required +0.002. One seed improved and two declined. Mean DRD2 performance increased by 0.034439, while sitagliptin decreased by 0.048248.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families and dense sulfur cages, with reactive bonds and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of the complete saved three-seed panels for this node and Parent n-abcd951ab7cc. Each objective contributes 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals; no objective lacks trajectories. The products range from compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds to larger decorated heteroaromatics, bridged amine/lactam frameworks and densely interconnected sulfur cages. Offline graph reading of the saved SMILES informs the size and ring descriptions; no new objective, drug-likeness or synthesis scores were calculated. The digest reports ring_closure_rate 1.0 for every proposal set. Aromatic-token presence rates in task order are 0.9586, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7299; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic atoms, not aromatic atom fractions or proof of aromaticity throughout a molecule. All sets have charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. There are recognizable indole carboxamides and aromatic amines, but also benzene-fused unsaturated four-member rings, peroxides, heteroatom-bound halogens and unusual multiple-bonded sulfur. The Parent comparison shows local changes within these broad families, including a sulfur-free bridged aromatic amine among the Child high scorers; it does not show uniform improvement in chemical plausibility. Structural diversity is moderate across the panel but much narrower within late seed trajectories: numerous distinct strings decorate related frameworks. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, with plausible-looking subsets and especially doubtful cage/sulfur subsets. All score-gradient statements below describe recorded associations. The available molecules do not establish a unique missing target scaffold or a causal contribution from an individual substituent.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer emits compact carbonyl-linked ring systems, with 20-29 heavy atoms on graph reading. Seed 1 retains an indole carboxanilide family with ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents; its recorded best at evaluation 61 is 0.39905049777278273 and is comparatively recognizable synthetic chemistry. Seeds 0 and 2 also reach benzene-fused unsaturated four-member carbocycles. The seed-0 best at evaluation 176, 0.4254027310763201, is an ester joining that strained fused framework to a methylpyridine, with a terminal enamine and fluoromethyl substituent. It is not an indene. Later seed-0 products include unusual sulfur-containing ring variants; seed-1 products acquire N-O bonds and awkward oxygen heterocycles; the final seed-2 cited amide carries an aryl hydroperoxide. The aromatic-token presence rate is 0.9586 and the cumulated-double-bond string rate is 0.1218, so this is ring-rich chemistry with appreciable unusual unsaturation.
liabilities: The best ester contains a benzene-fused unsaturated four-member ring and an enamine; ring strain and chemical stability are concerns even though the graph parses.

Other high entries use unusual sulfur multiple bonding, while low and late entries include N-O linkages, heteroatom-bound halogens or hydroperoxides. Their presence should not be equated with ordinary medicinal substituents.
The aryl thiol in the comparatively plausible indole example remains a reactive functional group; its good recorded score is not a synthesis or stability measurement.
missing_features: Consistent retention of ordinary fused aromatic carbonyl frameworks during later diversification is missing: the relatively conventional indole carboxamide is present, but later proposals frequently substitute strained annulation or disruptive heteroatom bonding.

The favorable compact carbonyl/aromatic pattern is not developed into a broad set of stable alternative attachment geometries. The trajectory cannot identify a particular absent heterocycle as the objective solution.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145; its simpler ethoxy/methyl/thiol relative reaches 0.39905049777278273. By comparison, the cited seed-0 carbonyl-disrupted, hydroxylamine-bearing analogue scores 0.03343008011310944, and the seed-1 N-hydroxy, extended oxygen-heterocycle amide scores 0.030639811858172862. Compact aromatic frameworks with a retained carbonyl connection fare better in these observations than those particular expanded or disrupted structures. This does not establish a universal benefit for sulfur or halogen substitution. Against the Parent, the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.393567030299894 in a benzothiophene ketone family to 0.4254027310763201 in the four-member-ring ester family; the seed-1 best molecule and score are unchanged, while seed 2 changes from 0.41003927643747895 to 0.3819619698458151. The higher seed-0 score therefore accompanies a more strained ring topology, rather than demonstrating easier synthesis.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest and most heavily decorated products in this panel: 30-53 heavy atoms in optimizer proposals, with aromatic atoms and ring-closure digits in every string. Seed 0 develops a fused pyrrole/pyrimidine carbonyl-thione system bearing imines and a long oxygen/sulfur-rich side chain. Its best cited molecule at evaluation 232 scores 0.6154582763337894 and includes a sulfur-chlorine terminus and unusual multiple-bonded sulfur. Seed 1 reaches an anilino aza-bicyclic aromatic family with an N-methyl diacyl nitrogen, a dimethylamino O,N-acetal side chain, a peroxide and an oxygen-chlorine group. Its maximum is 0.6165764586926783. Seed 2 retains a fused dicarbonyl heterocycle and oxygen/nitrogen ring decoration while acquiring thioethers, a thioacetal-like carbon and an allene-containing unsaturated chain; its maximum is 0.5933446875409407. The ordinary aromatic and carbonyl substructures are embedded in increasingly doubtful combinations of reactive groups.
liabilities: The leading seed-1 series combines a peroxide with an organic hypochlorite group; its O,N-acetal and activated diacyl nitrogen add further stability questions. An unsaturated acyl group is an electrophilic motif, not a demonstration of selective reactivity.
Seed-0 structures include sulfur-chlorine bonding, imines and unusual sulfur valence environments. Seed-2 structures add allene/polyene and sulfur-rich side chains.

The large number of substituents and unspecified configurations complicate synthetic interpretation. Equal recorded scores across reactive-group changes do not establish equivalence in real chemical behavior.
missing_features: The high-scoring aromatic/carbonyl framework lacks a well-developed set of chemically conservative peripheral variants. A recorded oxygen-chlorine replacement preserves the score, but peroxide-free and otherwise stable analogues of that same family are not established by the cited high-scoring set.

The output does not demonstrate control over side-chain complexity while retaining favorable ring and polar-group arrangements; the late products remain heavily decorated and chemically heterogeneous.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.548381482770623, whereas the cited early exocyclic-methylene/carbonyl-modified analogue scores 0.5286081645773063. Larger heteroaromatic structures with elaborated polar and alkyl decoration reach the higher recorded band, but the gradient is tolerant of chemically substantial peripheral changes. The cited seed-1 ethyl and methyl variants, and the analogue replacing oxygen-bound chlorine with a chloroethoxy chain, all score 0.6165764586926783. Thus the oxygen-chlorine bond is not required to retain that observed value in this family. Parent maxima for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.6161710037174721, 0.605139548855754 and 0.6092182584436399, respectively. The Child substitutes a peroxide-bearing aza-bicyclic family for the Parent seed-1 imine-rich aza-aromatic family and ends seed 2 in a more sulfur-decorated allene family. The score changes do not indicate a consistent move toward stable functionality.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are medium-to-large aromatic amine frameworks, with 30-43 heavy atoms on graph reading, aromatic-token presence 1.0 and halogen presence 0.9989. Early low scorers are oxygen-rich biaryl carboxylic acids carrying amide and N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine groups. Later seed-0 products contain small nitrogen rings, free amines and unusual sulfur linkages. Seed 1 reaches a sulfur-free bridged polyaromatic nitrogen framework with an aminoalkyl secondary amine, an aryl amino group, a phenol and chlorinated aryl/benzylic substitution; its best cited molecule scores 0.9420019982182398. Seed 2 instead reaches a chlorophenyl/fluoropyrrolidine amine assembly attached to a sulfur-rich fused ring system with an aminomethyl group and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds; its maximum is 0.9441493227693659. Basic amine functionality is clearly available to the generator, although no formal charged state is encoded.
liabilities: The sulfur-rich leaders contain unusual neutral sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and hydrogen-bearing sulfur environments; sanitization does not demonstrate isolable, conformationally feasible compounds.
The sulfur-free bridged leader still contains a benzylic chloride and an aryl amine, and its ring-junction configurations are unassigned.

Almost universal halogenation and the extensive aromatic surface make these hydrophobic frameworks rather than broadly balanced polar chemotypes; actual solubility or ionization cannot be read from the objective score.
missing_features: Explicit protonation-state and stereochemical alternatives for the amine-containing ring assemblies are absent from the supplied representation; the evidence does not show whether such alternatives would change the objective.

Chemically simpler ways of presenting the observed aromatic/amine arrangement are underdeveloped. The sulfur-free family is an existing foothold, while many other high entries keep unusual sulfur bonding or highly bridged topology.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited early acid/amide/sulfonamide structure scores 0.007468397818197266, compared with 0.9420019982182398 for the bridged aromatic aminoalkyl structure and 0.9441493227693659 for the sulfur-rich aminomethyl structure. The visible association favors aromatic hydrophobic surface arranged with non-amide amines and fewer acidic/carbonyl-rich appendages; atom count alone does not explain it. The two cited seed-2 leaders differ by a ring sulfur versus carbon and have the same 0.9441493227693659 score, so that particular extra sulfur is not required for the observed maximum. The Parent-to-Child seed maxima are unchanged at 0.8856242185485628 for seed 0, change from 0.868020189804352 to 0.9420019982182398 for seed 1, and from 0.9148143511682032 to 0.9441493227693659 for seed 2. Seed 1 supplies a real sulfur-free high-scoring family, but the persistent bridged topology and reactive substituents still limit synthetic confidence. These scores alone do not establish a binding pose or interaction mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The products combine aromatic groups with lactam/urea-derived and bridged heterocyclic frameworks, spanning 27-43 heavy atoms in optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and aromatic-token presence are both 1.0. Seed 0 develops a compact, densely bridged pyridine/phenyl system with a tertiary lactam and an N-O bridge; the best cited molecule at evaluation 196 scores 0.21196904390980506. Seed 1 retains a brominated aromatic/thioester family and later oxygen-bromine and sulfur-rich ring derivatives; its maximum is 0.19092251395438758. Seed 2 develops larger oxygen/nitrogen-containing ring assemblies with lactam and ketone functionality, then unusual sulfur junctions; its maximum is 0.20784255919268485. The late cited seed-2 molecules additionally carry an aryl hydroperoxide. Some components are ordinary medicinal chemistry, but the complete bridge networks and heteroatom combinations have questionable synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: N-O bridges, multiple shared ring junctions and larger heterocyclic loops leave substantial conformational and stereochemical uncertainty.

Oxygen-bromine groups, hydroperoxides, hydrazine-like connections and unusual sulfur environments appear in the cited output. These are real features of the proposed chemistry, not evidence of synthetic accessibility.
The high number of distinct strings includes close variations of recurring bridged families; it does not establish broad coverage of practical scaffolds.
missing_features: The favorable aromatic/lactam arrangement is not explored as a broad family of ordinary, stereochemically defined ring frameworks; late variation largely elaborates dense bridges and unusual heteroatom connections.

The data do not demonstrate a clean structural compromise that raises the recorded band while simplifying the bridge network. More rings or more sulfur cannot be identified as a generally missing objective requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.1678386594791329. The cited ring-opened, extended urea/hydrazine analogue scores 0.12467972074136988, while the constrained seed-0 lactam/N-O-bridged system reaches 0.21196904390980506. This supports an association with particular constrained aromatic/polar arrangements, not a general preference for maximum ring count. The seed-1 oxygen-bromine/sulfur compound with an opened polar chain scores 0.12870267321446027. Reactive groups also survive in high entries: the cited seed-0 peroxide-bridge variant scores 0.20647766243219587 and the seed-2 aryl-hydroperoxide variant scores 0.20769510081357428. Parent best molecules and maxima are retained in seeds 0 and 1; seed 2 changes from 0.20185639717998205 in an oxygen/nitrogen-rich ring assembly to 0.20784255919268485 in a sulfur-containing derivative. The recorded improvement is therefore compatible with persistent chemical liabilities.

per_task.generated_character: These are compact but densely interconnected sulfur-rich cages, with 25-33 heavy atoms in optimizer proposals. Aromatic-token presence is 0.7299, yet the cited best molecules from seeds 0 and 2 have no aromatic atoms on graph reading; ring density must not be confused with aromaticity. The seed-0 best at evaluation 260 scores 0.48118636011729826 and combines small unsaturated rings, repeated hydrogen-bearing sulfur junctions, a carbonyl, fluoromethyl and acyl fluoride groups, and a sulfur-oxygen/nitrogen substituent. The seed-1 best at evaluation 294 scores 0.4456072955728387 and contains a thio-ring network, a residual aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl ring, N-chlorine and sulfur-fluorine bonding. The seed-2 best at evaluation 297 scores 0.4484554129767839 and combines sulfur bridges, small rings, a carbonyl, aldehyde and N-fluoro amidine-like group. These high-scoring structures are among the least convincing synthetic products in the panel.
liabilities: Small unsaturated rings, heavily shared junctions and unusual neutral sulfur valence environments make conformational feasibility and practical synthesis especially doubtful.
Acyl fluorides, N-fluorinated or N-chlorinated nitrogen, sulfur-fluorine groups and aldehydes create reactive chemistry in combinations whose stability is unestablished.

Configurations at substituted cage junctions and possible stereogenic heteroatom environments are unspecified. A graph-valid string and a positive objective score do not resolve those structures into experimentally characterized molecules.
missing_features: The high-scoring set does not supply chemically ordinary, stereochemically resolved scaffolds that test the compact polar/carbonyl arrangements without the dense sulfur framework.

Stable placement of fluorine and nitrogen functionality is underdeveloped: much of the shown variation binds halogens to nitrogen or sulfur, or uses acyl fluorides, rather than establishing a coherent family with conventional carbon-bound substituents. The trajectory does not identify a specific absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.0020944534688323298, and its cited early ring-expanded carbonyl analogue scores 7.590554525032884e-10. Much higher values occur after dense sulfur-ring restructuring and changes in carbonyl/fluorine placement. This is not a smooth reward for sulfur or ring count: the cited sulfur-rich seed-1 molecule at evaluation 248 still scores only 3.04809716642635e-09, and the final seed-2 ring/linker-expanded variant at evaluation 298 scores 0.01685401516576383 beside the evaluation-297 maximum of 0.4484554129767839. These compounds differ in connectivity, so an isolated substituent effect cannot be assigned. The Parent and Child retain the same best molecules and scores in seeds 0 and 2; seed 1 changes from a different sulfur-rich cage scoring 0.5903526424693334 to the N-chlorinated cage scoring 0.4456072955728387. The chemical family remains highly unconventional even where scores differ substantially.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High and late digest molecules include peroxides, oxygen-bound chlorine or bromine, nitrogen-bound fluorine or chlorine, and sulfur-chlorine groups alongside ordinary amides, ethers and amines. In one cited high-scoring aromatic series, replacing oxygen-bound chlorine with a chloroethoxy chain retains exactly the same recorded score. Reactive functionality is therefore sometimes tolerated without being necessary for that observed value.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically stable functional-group identities while diversifying otherwise recognizable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs chemically coherent alternatives for local functional-group changes, including stable replacements that preserve the surrounding attachment geometry. Apply any chemical plausibility treatment through general local chemistry, and let observed feedback determine which variants matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0. The cited compact ester leaders contain a benzene-fused unsaturated four-member ring; other high entries are densely bridged lactam frameworks or sulfur cages with small unsaturated rings. Their favorable recorded scores coexist with substantial uncertainty about conformational feasibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator explores ring closure abundantly but does not demonstrate reliable control of realistic ring strain and junction geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring proposals need access to chemically credible attachment topologies and junction arrangements, with strain-sensitive structural checks or coherent ring replacements. This is a need for control over which ring systems are produced, rather than for more ring-closure events.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in every digest proposal set, including the amine-containing saturated rings, multiply substituted cage junctions and bridged lactam structures. The cited high scorers likewise carry no explicit tetrahedral configuration tags.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no demonstrated stereochemical resolution of the substituted and bridged structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: To represent chemically distinct products fully, the generator would need to recognize genuinely stereogenic environments and preserve or enumerate compatible configurations without changing scaffold connectivity. The current observations establish missing representation, not an objective-score benefit from adding it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited output includes primary aminomethyl groups, secondary aminoalkyl linkers, tertiary amines and aza-aromatic nitrogens, yet charged_rate is 0.0 in every proposal set. Neutral notation alone does not establish the solution protonation state, nor does it mean the generator lacks basic centers.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable amine functionality is available, but explicit chemical-state coverage is not demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation could distinguish relevant charge and protonation states while preserving chemical identity and avoiding redundant state proposals. Any usefulness would have to be checked against the actual scoring interface; it cannot be inferred from the absence of charge marks.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains 879 unique molecules in most proposal-plus-initial task pools and 877 in the remaining pool, but late seed trajectories repeatedly decorate related carbonyl-linked aromatics, bridged amine/lactam frameworks or sulfur cages. Comparatively conventional indole carboxamides and a sulfur-free bridged aromatic amine are present, showing that ordinary chemistry is accessible but not consistently developed.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct output strings do not yet amount to broad coverage of chemically credible scaffold families around favorable motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broader exploration would require coherent alternatives to the recurring ring and linker frameworks while retaining useful functional-group arrangements. Scaffold and attachment diversity should be assessed chemically, rather than treating every new graph string as evidence of a new practical chemotype.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
